primary_question: Which organisms are plausible causes of the index pneumonia episode?
inclusion: Organisms explicitly adjudicated as causes of the index pneumonia episode.
Respiratory-specimen diagnoses linked to the index episode.
Blood, plasma, or sterile-site organisms only when a blinded clinical adjudicator links the same organism and event to pneumonia.
exclusion: Organisms explicitly labeled urine-only, urinary-tract-only, stool-only, wound-only, or another nonpulmonary episode without pneumonia linkage.
Colonization, contamination, resolved prior infection, and asymptomatic shedding when explicitly documented.
Organisms inferred as pulmonary only because the model predicted them.
ambiguous: Unqualified bloodstream or plasma diagnoses without an episode link require blinded physician adjudication.
Unqualified workbook diagnoses remain unresolved rather than being reclassified from model output.
leakage_controls: Adjudication must be performed without seeing model tier, rule, or benchmark outcome.
The raw all-clinical-pathogen contract remains immutable and is never overwritten.
Pulmonary-only labels are a separate sensitivity endpoint with source and reason for every inclusion or exclusion.
